 ORDER

sentences.text: The present appeal has been filed by Smt. Purnima Nigam, W/o Shri Satish Chandra Nigam and mother of Shri Abhishek Nigam.

3. A claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act was filed before the Court of First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal which was registered as Claim Case No.553/2006 against Abhishek Nigam, M/s HIG Limited and The Oriental Insurance Company Limited.

entities.text: Court of First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Abhishek Nigam was alleged to be driving the offending vehicle.
Abhishek Nigam did not appear before the Claims Tribunal and he was proceeded ex parte.

By award dated 24.10.2007 passed in Claim Case No.553/2006, it was held that only Abhishek Nigam is liable to pay the compensation of Rs.4,88,300/- with interest @ 6% from the date of filing of the claim petition.
4. It appears that Abhishek Nigam died on 24.11.2010.

Thereafter, on 21.12.2016 the appellant filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of CPC on the ground that her son Abhishek Nigam was non-applicant in the claim petition and he did not contest the said claim petition.

Since Abhishek Nigam had performed love marriage with a South Indian girl, therefore, on 30.08.2008 an information was sent to D.I.G., District Bhopal with regard to breaking of relationship by the appellant with Abhishek Nigam and in this regard, a public notice was also published in a Daily Newspaper dated 15.11.2008.
It was alleged that after the marriage Abhishek Nigam shifted to Kerala alongwith his wife.
It was claimed that the appellant and respondent No.8 have no relationship with Abhishek Nigam from the month of January, 2003.

It was further mentioned that earlier her son Abhishek Nigam was involved in antisocial activities and accordingly, the appellant and respondent No.8 broke their relationship with Abhishek Nigam in the month of January, 2003 and in this regard news was also published in Daily Raj Express on 08.06.2007.
It was further alleged that Abhishek Nigam was not the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
It was claimed that from the month of January, 2003 the appellant and respondent No.8 had no relationship with Abhishek Nigam.

Since Abhishek Nigam had performed marriage with a South Indian girl,
therefore, now the wife of Abhishek Nigam is the legal representative and the appellant and respondent No.8 are not the legal representative of Abhishek Nigam.

It was further alleged that the award which has been passed against Abhishek Nigam may not be executed against the appellant and accordingly, it was prayed that since the appellant was not a party to the claim petition,
therefore, the ex parte award be set aside and she may be heard.
5.

The application was opposed by counsel for defendants Nos.2 to 5.
6.
The Claims Tribunal by impugned order dated 13.12.2019 passed in MJC No.642/2016 rejected the application.

7. Challenging the order passed by the Court below, it is submitted by the counsel for the appellant that since Abhishek Nigam had performed his marriage with a South Indian girl, therefore, the appellant and respondent No.1 had broken their relationship with Abhishek Nigam and a public notice was also published in the Daily Newspaper on 15.11.2008.
It is further submitted that another public notice was issued in the newspaper with regard to breaking of ties due to antisocial activities Purnima Nigam vs Smt. Kanchan Pathak on 9 May, 2023

3 of son of the appellant and thus, it is clear that the appellant and respondent No.8 are not the legal representatives.

It is further submitted that since Abhishek Nigam had not contested the claim petition, therefore, the appellant may be permitted to contest the claim petition and accordingly, it is prayed that the ex parte award passed against Abhishek Nigam be set aside.
8.
Per contra, the appeal is vehemently opposed by the counsel for respondents Nos.1, 2, 3 & 5.

It is submitted by the counsel for respondents Nos.1, 2, 3 & 5 that Abhishek Nigam was duly served in the claim case and he did not appear before the Claims Tribunal and accordingly, he was proceeded ex parte.
The award was passed on 24.10.2007.
According to the appellant, Abhishek Nigam has expired on 24.11.2010.
Although it has been claimed by the appellant that Abhishek Nigam has performed marriage with a South Indian girl but she has not disclosed the address and name of the said girl.
9. It appears that the allegation of marrying a South Indian girl is an afterthought.
Even otherwise marrying a girl of different caste is not an offence and it is also not void or voidable marriage under the Hindu Marriage Act.

As per Section 8 of Hindu Succession Act, the mother is the Class I heir of Abhishek Nigam and thus, it is clear that the appellant has failed to make out any ground for setting aside the ex parte award.

10. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
11.

It is the case of the appellant that since Abhishek Nigam had performed marriage with a South Indian girl and had shifted to Kerala, therefore, the appellant as well as respondent No.1 had broken their ties with Abhishek Nigam.
12. The counsel for the appellant could not point out as to how marrying a girl of different caste is an offence or is void or voidable marriage under the provisions of Hindu Succession Act.

Furthermore,
the appellant has not disclosed the name of the girl as well as has not disclosed the address of the girl with whom Abhishek Nigam had allegedly performed marriage.
Thus, it is clear that the allegation of marriage of Abhishek Nigam with a South Indian girl is an afterthought.
The impugned award was passed on 24.10.2007 and the public notice was published by the appellant in this regard in the Newspaper dated 15.11.2008.
Thus, a public notice with regard to breaking of ties with Abhishek Nigam was published after the award was passed.
Therefore, it is clear that the public notice dated 15.11.2008 is an afterthought and is based on ill-advice.

13. Be that whatever it may be.
14.

Since the appellant had not disclosed the name of so called wife of Abhishek Nigam, therefore, it is not possible for this Court to accept that Abhishek Nigam had performed marriage with South Indian girl and had shifted to Kerala.
According to Section 8 as well as Schedule under Hindu Succession Act, the mother is a Class 1 heir.

Furthermore, when Abhishek Nigam did not participate in the claim petition and decided to stay away from the Claims Tribunal and in absence of any averment that Abhishek Nigam was not served with a notice in the claim petition, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal did not commit any mistake by rejecting the Purnima Nigam vs Smt. 4 application filed by the appellant for the simple reason that she cannot seek the reopening of the claim petition on the ground that she was not a party and her son, who was a party did not contest the claim petition.

sentences.text: 15. No reason has been assigned by the appellant as to why Abhishek Nigam did not appear before the Claims Tribunal.
From the award which was passed against Abhishek Nigam it is clear that the accident took place in the year 2005 and we are in 2023.
Even after 18 years of the accident, it appears that the compensation amount could not be paid to the claimants.

16. Be that whatever it may be.
17.
It is next contended by the counsel for the appellant that the appellant was made a party to the execution proceeding without giving an opportunity of hearing.
18. Undisputedly, the appellant is the mother of deceased Abhishek Nigam.

This Court has already come to a conclusion that in the light of Section 8 as well as Schedule under Hindu Succession Act,
mother is Class I heir.
19.
Even during the course of argument, the counsel for the appellant could not convince the Court as to how she can claim that she is not a Class I heir of Abhishek Nigam.
20. Further in view of Section 50 of CPC, a decree can be executed against the legal heir of the judgment debtor.
21. Under these circumstances, no case is made out warranting interference.
22. The appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
